appendix.authoring_note: definition, raw_source, units, default_behavior, higher_value_meaning and known_caveats are intentionally blank. They are claims about the domain, not properties derivable from the model, and inventing them would produce documentation that reads as authoritative and is not.

training_window.detail: a separate fit per test year, each on 2010 through the year before it -- 12 fits in all
training_window.sentence: These are walk-forward figures, not one model's: for each test year the model was fitted on 2010 through the previous year and then scored that year, so the result concatenates 12 separately fitted models and no test year appears in its own training data. The window expands each year, so the last year's model saw the most data and the first year's the least.

identity.comparator_note: The market's own implied probabilities on the same races. Every published report is scored against the market, so the four headline numbers mean the same thing and can be read against one another. For the production model the market is also the baseline by construction -- the booster learns a residual on log(market_prob) -- and for the probit candidates it is the common yardstick rather than the quantity they were designed against; the comparison each was designed against is in the technical appendix.
identity.label: Bagged Offset (production)

delta_semantics.definition: model race log loss minus market race log loss, paired by race

run.refusal_note: Refusals are recorded rather than omitted, so a reader can see the strategy was considered and declined. Rebate-aware sizing cannot reuse stale bankroll-dependent fractions on a divergent path.

refused.reason: rebate_aware_sizing makes the Kelly threshold fraction depend on the current bankroll, so fractions solved on the historical path are stale on any simulated path that diverges from it. Reusing them would give confidently wrong risk numbers biased in an unknown direction. Re-solve per replicate or exclude this strategy.
